answer: An agent economy can deter sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before earning reputation or claiming work. If it misses a verifiable deadline, the protocol burns part of that bond; honest completion returns it. A hundred fake identities thus tie up a hundred bonds and risk losing capital when challenged. This is not proof of personhood, but it makes deception expensive: an orchard of fakes must cross a canyon of locked funds and face the reef of slashing.
